rows.speaker: الأصحاب
rows.claim: The proponents infer that God makes obedience more likely for believers and sin more likely for disbelievers, so the favored side becomes necessary.
rows.anchor: استدل الأصحاب بهذه الآية على صحة قولهم في التوفيق والخذلان

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: The wording may use one opposite for another: enabling good is ease toward good, while withholding such aids is ease toward hardship.
rows.anchor: أجاب القفال رحمه الله عن

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: The verse may attribute an outcome to its cause, as the idols are said to have led many people astray.
rows.anchor: أجاب القفال رحمه الله عن

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: The wording may be a divine judgment and report about the person's end.
rows.anchor: أجاب القفال رحمه الله عن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects all three replies as departures from the apparent meaning, which he says is reinforced by decisive rational proof.
rows.anchor: عن الكل أنه عدول عن الظاهر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from ʿAli says every soul's place in Paradise or Hell is known to God; when asked whether people should then rely on fate, the Prophet said to act, since each is facilitated toward what it was created for.
rows.anchor: عن علي عليه السلام عن النبي

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal answers that all people were created to worship God, citing the statement that jinn and humans were created for worship.
rows.anchor: أجاب القفال عنه بأن الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi calls this answer weak: the Prophet's reply means each person is facilitated toward what accords with God's prior knowledge, which cannot change.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذا ضعيف لأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future particle may promise divine gentleness and guidance with certainty, as in the command to worship so that people may become mindful.
rows.anchor: أنه على سبيل الترفيق والتلطيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future wording may leave room for moral change: an obedient person may sin, while a sinner may repent and obey.
rows.anchor: أن يحمل ذلك على أن المطيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future may mark delay because most reward comes in the afterlife, whose time is known only to God.
rows.anchor: أن الثواب لما كان أكثره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle ما can be either a rhetorical question of denial or a plain negation.
rows.anchor: ما هنا يحتمل أن يكون استفهاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of تردى derives it from falling: the miser falls into the grave or Hell, where the wealth he left heirs cannot help him.
rows.anchor: أن يكون ذلك مأخوذا من قولك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealth left behind does not accompany its owner; only charitable deeds and wealth spent in its proper rights benefit him in the next life.
rows.anchor: الذي بخل به وتركه لوارثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, تردى is derived from destruction and means death.
rows.anchor: أن تردى تفعل من الردى وهو الهلاك يريد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لظى means a fire that blazes, flares, and burns intensely; Hell is named لظى from this quality.
rows.anchor: تلظى أي تتوقد وتتلهب وتتوهج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the passage was revealed about Umayya ibn Khalaf and others who denied Muhammad and earlier prophets.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أمية بن خلف وأمثاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective الأشقى can mean simply wretched: only the disbeliever who denied God's signs and turned from obedience enters this particular fire.
rows.anchor: إن الأشقى بمعنى الشقي كما يقال

rows.speaker: المرجئة
rows.claim: The Murjiʾa cite the verse to argue that the threat of Hell applies only to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن المرجئة يتمسكون بهذه الآية في أنه لا وعيد إلا على الكفار

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi argues the apparent reading wrongly exempts sinful unbelievers who neither deny nor turn away from Hell.
rows.anchor: أنه يقتضي أن لا يدخل النار

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi says this reading would entice people to sin, as though believers could commit any sin without consequence.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : ولا يمكن إجراء هذه الآية

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi argues that the next verse also excludes sinners from salvation, since a grave sinner cannot be called the most God-fearing.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : ولا يمكن إجراء هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi judges the Qadi's objections weak, though he says the apparent wording must be interpreted.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن وجوه القاضي ضعيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation restricts لظى to a particular level of Hell, which only the most wretched enters; sinful people may enter other levels.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse refers to all Hell and says the denier is most entitled to it, without denying that other sinners enter it.
rows.anchor: وثبوت هذه الزيادة في الاستحقاق غير حاصل إلا لهذا الأشقى

none: Only the quoted verses 92:17-19 are present; the segment gives no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes take الضحى either as the midmorning, when the sun rises and spreads its light, or as the whole daytime, contrasted with the whole night.
rows.anchor: المراد بالضحى وقت الضحى وهو صدر النهار

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد والمبرد والزجاج
rows.claim: They explain سجى as becoming still, as in a calm night, still eye, or sea whose waves have settled; a poetic line applies the word to the sea.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو عبيد والمبرد والزجاج : سجى أي سكن

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ explains سجى as becoming dark and settled through the night.
rows.anchor: سجى أي أظلم وركد في طوله

rows.speaker: الأصمعي وابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿi and Ibn al-Aʿrabi explain the night as covering the day, like a person covered with a garment.
rows.anchor: فقال الأصمعي وابن الأعرابي سجى الليل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says night covers the world with darkness; in another report through Saʿid ibn Jubayr, its onset covers everything.
rows.anchor: غطى الدنيا بالظلمة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says night clothes people in its darkness.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والسدي وابن زيد
rows.claim: They explain the night as stilling people, either by metonymy or because its darkness has settled and become complete.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة والسدي وابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reason for reversing the night-day order across the two suras is that each has a distinct merit: night comes first, while daylight brings light; alternating them also balances the sequence.
rows.anchor: بالليل والنهار ينتظم مصالح المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation links the previous sura's night to Abu Bakr, whose past included disbelief, and this sura's daylight to Muhammad, who had no prior sin.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى قدم الليل على النهار في سورة أبي بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation identifies the two suras with Abu Bakr and Muhammad and says their consecutive order shows no intermediary between them.
rows.anchor: سورة والليل سورة أبي بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternation of day and night shows that pauses in revelation follow wisdom, just as the shifting hours do not reflect divine whim or rejection.
rows.anchor: فمرة تزداد ساعات الليل وتنقص ساعات النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the disbelievers claimed that God abandoned and hated the Prophet, their unsupported charge is answered by a divine oath, as a claimant is asked for proof and the denier swears.
rows.anchor: هاتوا الحجة فعجزوا فلزمه اليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternating night and day show that neither is free from the other; likewise people should not expect exemption from hardship.
rows.anchor: انظروا إلى جوار الليل مع النهار لا يسلم أحدهما عن الآخر بل الليل تارة يغلب وتارة يغلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midmorning is when people gather and find ease after the isolation of night, so it promises revelation and comfort after the Prophet's anxiety during its pause.
rows.anchor: أنه وقت اجتماع الناس وكمال الأنس بعد الاستيحاش في زمان الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midmorning recalls the hour Moses spoke with God and the sorcerers prostrated; the God who honored Moses can honor Muhammad and turn his enemies' hearts.
rows.anchor: أنها الساعة التي كلم فيها موسى ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A brief daylight hour set against the whole night suggests Muhammad's stature equals all prophets and that worldly grief lasts longer than joy; an anecdote pictures sorrow lasting centuries and joy an hour.
rows.anchor: أن ساعة من النهار توازي جميع الليل كما أن محمدا إذا وزن يوازي جميع الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Busy daylight resembles resurrection and quiet night resembles the stillness of graves; life and the postmortem state are more excellent than death and what precedes it.
rows.anchor: وقت الضحى وقت حركة الناس وتعارفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning midmorning first prevents despair of God's relief, while following it with night prevents complacency about His plan.
rows.anchor: ذكروا الضحى حتى لا يحصل اليأس من روحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes take midmorning as Muhammad's face and night as his hair; others interpret them as the male and female members of his family.
rows.anchor: فسر الضحى بوجه محمد والليل بشعره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other symbolic readings make midmorning Muhammad's mission and night the pause in revelation, which brought estrangement after the comfort of revelation.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل الضحى رسالته والليل زمان احتباس الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midmorning can symbolize the light of Muhammad's knowledge that reveals hidden matters, and night his forgiving concealment of faults.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل والضحى نور علمه الذي به يعرف المستور من الغيوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pair may symbolize Islam's initial rise from strangeness and its later return to strangeness.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن الضحى إقبال الإسلام بعد أن كل غريبا والليل إشارة إلى أنه سيعود غريبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes midmorning full intellect and night the state of death.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل والضحى كمال العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath may refer to Muhammad's outward and inward selves, neither of which the unseen knows to be flawed.
rows.anchor: أقسم بعلانيتك التي لا يرى عليها الخلق عيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waddaʿaka derives from farewell; its lighter reading means He did not leave you, while qila means hatred and intensifies the idea of abandonment.
rows.anchor: ودعك من التوديع كما يودع المفارق

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ explains the omitted object in وما قلى as understood from the preceding كاف; omitting it also preserves the verse endings.
rows.anchor: وفي حذف الكاف وجوه أحدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving the object unexpressed may broaden the assurance: God hates neither the Prophet nor his companions or those he loves until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ولا أحدا ممن أحبك إلى قيام القيامة

rows.speaker: المشركون
rows.claim: When Gabriel's arrival was delayed, the polytheists claimed that God had abandoned and hated Muhammad.
rows.anchor: أبطأ جبريل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the revelation pause lasted forty nights and that Khadija suggested the Lord might have forgotten or hated him.
rows.anchor: أبطأ عليه أربعين ليلة فشكا ذلك إلى خديجة

rows.speaker: أم جميل
rows.claim: Umm Jamil, Abu Lahab's wife, told Muhammad that his devil seemed to have left him.
rows.anchor: إن أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب قالت له

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reports that Muhammad told Khadija his Lord had abandoned and hated him; she reassured him that God would complete the honor He began.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الحسن أنه قال : أبطأ على الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم الوحي ، فقال لخديجة

rows.speaker: الأصوليون
rows.claim: Theologians reject that report as incompatible with a prophet knowing that God would not remove his mission and that revelation's timing follows wisdom.
rows.anchor: وطعن الأصوليون في هذه الرواية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the report is sound, Muhammad's remark can be understood as testing Khadija's understanding or showing people her knowledge.
rows.anchor: ثم إن صح ذلك يحمل على أنه كان مقصوده عليه الصلاة والسلام أن يجربها ليعرف قدر علمها

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj gives the revelation pause as twelve days; al-Kalbi says fifteen, Ibn ʿAbbas twenty-five, and al-Suddi and Muqatil forty.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن جريج : اثنا عشر يوما

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Most exegetes say the pause followed Muhammad's promise to answer questions about the Spirit, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Companions of the Cave without saying God willing.
rows.anchor: فذكر أكثر المفسرين أن اليهود سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الروح وذي القرنين وأصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd attributes the delay to a puppy in the home of al-Hasan and al-Husayn; Gabriel said angels do not enter a house containing a dog or image.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد : السبب فيه كون جرو

rows.speaker: جندب بن سفيان
rows.claim: Jundub ibn Sufyan says a stone struck Muhammad finger, after which revelation paused.
rows.anchor: وقال جندب بن سفيان : رمى النبي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says Muhammad told Gabriel that he had missed him and longed for him; Gabriel replied that he longed for Muhammad even more but was a commanded servant.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال لجبريل : ( ما جثتني حتى اشتقت إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted line presents the Prophet as accepting a bleeding finger in Gods cause, after which revelation paused.
rows.anchor: هل أنت إلا أصبع دميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pause does not imply hatred: at most it reflected leaving the better course, which does not make its recipient hated; a report has Muhammad say he longed for Gabriel, who replied that he was even more eager but commanded, citing 19:64.
rows.anchor: السؤال الأول : الروايات التي ذكرتم تدل على أن احتباس الوحي كان عن قلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An assurance that a ruler does not hate a close servant would not ordinarily be needed, but answers enemies' rumor and honors the distressed recipient.
rows.anchor: السؤال الثاني : كيف يحسن من السلطان أن يقول لأعظم الخلق قربة عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode shows that the Qur'an comes from God: if Muhammad had composed it himself, revelation would not have been withheld from him.
rows.anchor: لكن الأعداء إذا ألقوا في الألسنة أن السلطان يبغضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also reported that a person among them did not trim his nails, another suggested cause for the delayed revelation.
rows.anchor: المسألة الثالثة : هذه الواقعة تدل على أن القرآن من عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's raising of Muhammad's renown includes fame on earth and in heaven, his name on the Throne and alongside God's name in testimony, prayer, and scripture.
rows.anchor: وشهرته في الأرض والسموات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His renown spreads through sermons, calls to prayer, letters, Qur'an, and earlier scriptures; God calls him Messenger or Prophet while naming Moses and Jesus directly.
rows.anchor: وأنه ختمت به النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes people love mentioning Muhammad, praise him, pray for him, and preserve his Sunna; each ritual prayer joins an obligatory act to his practice.
rows.anchor: وأيضا جعله في القلوب بحيث يستطيبون ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obeying and pledging allegiance to Muhammad count as obeying and pledging allegiance to God.
rows.anchor: وجعلت طاعتك طاعتي وبيعتك بيعتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His honor endures through readers, exegetes, preachers, scholars, rulers, and people seeking his intercession and blessing at his resting place.
rows.anchor: فالقراء يحفظون ألفاظ منشورك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses console Muhammad after Meccan polytheists mocked his poverty and offered to make him wealthy; he feared poverty was why they rejected Islam.
rows.anchor: أن المشركين كانوا يعيرون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding reminders of divine favor lead to a promise of worldly ease; the initial فاء connects this assurance to the Prophet's distress.
rows.anchor: فعدد الله تعالى عليه مننه في هذه السورة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says God made one hardship between two eases, so one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يقول الله تعالى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Muqatil transmits from the Prophet the saying that one hardship will not overcome two eases, followed by a recitation of the verses.
rows.anchor: مقاتل عن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه قال

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: They argue that definite العسر repeated refers to the same hardship, while indefinite يسرا repeated can denote two distinct eases.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء والزجاج : العسر

rows.speaker: الجرجاني
rows.claim: Al-Jurjani rejects that grammatical inference: repeating a sentence about a horse and sword does not necessarily mean one horse has two swords.
rows.anchor: وزيف الجرجاني هذا وقال : إذا قال الرجل : إن مع الفارس سيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the second sentence repeats the first to implant and reinforce its meaning, like the repeated warning woe to deniers.
rows.anchor: أن تكون الجملة الثانية تكريرا للأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two eases may be worldly victory and the reward of Paradise, as in the promise of one of two good outcomes.
rows.anchor: يسر الدنيا وهو ما تيسر من استفتاح البلاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite ease conveys magnificence: the meaning is an immense, extraordinary ease.
rows.anchor: معنى التنكير في اليسر ؟ جوابه : التفخيم ، كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ease follows hardship so soon and with such certainty that it is treated as accompanying it, although opposites do not literally coexist.
rows.anchor: كان وقوع اليسر بعد العسر بزمان قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To explain why God swears by apparently ordinary fruits, one view takes fig and olive literally; Ibn ʿAbbas says they are the familiar local fruits.
rows.anchor: المراد من التين والزيتون هذان الشيآن المشهوران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fig is described as food, fruit, and medicine; physicians attribute digestive, laxative, and other bodily benefits to it.
rows.anchor: أما التين فقالوا إنه غذاء وفاكهة ودواء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says a plate of figs was brought to the Prophet, who called them a fruit from Paradise, seedless, and beneficial for hemorrhoids and gout.
rows.anchor: وروى أنه أهدي لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم طبق من تين

rows.speaker: علي بن موسى الرضا
rows.claim: ʿAli al-Rida says figs freshen the mouth, lengthen hair, protect against paralysis, and can be used to expel bodily excess.
rows.anchor: وعن علي بن موسى الرضا عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike fruits whose outer and inner parts differ in quality, the fig is good both outside and inside.
rows.anchor: أما التين فإنه طيب الظاهر والباطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fig bears fruit before showing flowers or leaves; unlike other trees, it gives before displaying itself, an image of generosity that al-Razi compares to the Prophet's selflessness and the Anṣar.
rows.anchor: وشجرة تبذل قبل الوعد ، وهي التين

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A saying compares other trees to the instruction to begin with oneself and dependents, while the fig tree resembles the Chosen Prophet, who begins with others.
rows.anchor: فسائر الأشجار كأرباب المعاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike other trees, a fig tree can produce another crop after its fruit falls in the same year.
rows.anchor: أن سائر الأشجار إذا اسقطت الثمرة من موضعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In dream interpretation, a fig signifies a good, wealthy man; receiving it predicts wealth and abundance, while eating it predicts children.
rows.anchor: أن التين في النوم رجل خير غني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports say Adam covered himself with fig leaves after disobedience; a second tale says the first gazelles he fed gained beauty and musk, while later greedy ones gained only beauty.
rows.anchor: روى أن آدم عليه السلام لما عصى وفارقته ثيابه تستر بورق التين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The olive tree is blessed: it serves as fruit, condiment, and medicine, needs little cultivation, and produces oil for both food and lamps.
rows.anchor: وأما الزيتون فشجرته هي الشجرة المباركة فاكهة من وجه وإدام من وجه ودواء من وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dreaming of an olive leaf signifies holding firmly to the strongest handhold; Ibn Sirin advises a sick dreamer to eat olives after interpreting a cryptic vision.
rows.anchor: من أخذ ورق الزيتون في المنام استمسك بالعروة الوثقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi prefers the literal fruits, concluding that their great benefits are the reason God swears by them.
rows.anchor: ثم قال المفسرون : التي والزيتون اسم لهذين المأكولين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The fig and olive may name two mountains in the Holy Land; their regions evoke prophetic origins, with Jesus, Israelite prophets, Moses, and Muhammad associated with the sites in sequence.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هما جبلان من الأرض المقدسة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: A second view takes the names as mosques: Ibn Zayd identifies them as the Damascus mosque and the Jerusalem mosque.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد : التين مسجد دمشق

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Other mosque identifications are the mosque of the Cave Companions and Ilya; Ibn ʿAbbas instead names Noah's mosque on al-Judi and the Jerusalem mosque.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : التين مسجد أصحاب أهل الكف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who read the terms as mosques prefer swearing by worship places, and say the place names stand for regions rich in figs and olives.
rows.anchor: والقائلون بهذا القول إنما ذهبوا إليه لأن القسم بالمسجد أحسن لأنه موضع العبادة والطاعة

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: A third view takes fig as Damascus and olive as Jerusalem; Shahr ibn Hawshab instead identifies Kufa and Syria, while al-Rabiʿ names mountains between Hamadan and Hulwan.
rows.anchor: فقال كعب : التين دمشق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The country readings may honor lands revered by Jews, Christians, Muslims, and Quraysh, or distinguish Damascus and Jerusalem's worldly blessings from Sinai and Mecca's religious blessings.
rows.anchor: لأن اليهود والنصارى والمسلمين ومشركي قريش كل واحد منهم يعظم بلدة من هذه البلاد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Sinai is the mountain where God spoke to Moses; Ibn ʿAbbas, through ʿIkrima, says Sinin means beautiful in Ethiopian.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس في رواية عكرمة : { الطور } الجبل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Sinin means blessed; al-Kalbi calls it a wooded mountain, and Muqatil says it is any fruit-bearing mountain in Nabataean.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : { وطور سينين } المبارك

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi prefers Sinin as the place name of the mountain; its name signifies beauty or blessing, and it cannot be an adjective because it is annexed to طور.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : والأولى أن يكون سينين اسما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure city is Mecca; أمين can mean safe or trustworthy, including a place whose entrants are protected from danger.
rows.anchor: فالمراد مكة والأمين : الآمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca is secure because God protected it from the Elephant, and because people, game, and animals are safe there when they seek refuge.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى حفظه عن الفيل على ما يأتيك شرحه إن شاء الله تعالى

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: ʿAli tells ʿUmar that the Black Stone can testify: at the primordial covenant it had a tongue, lips, and eyes, swallowed the written covenant, and bears witness to pilgrims until Judgment.
rows.anchor: فقال له علي عليه السلام : إما أنه يضر وينفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human refers to the human kind; taqwim means shaping and adjusting something into the form it ought to have.
rows.anchor: المراد من الإنسان هذه الماهية والتقويم تصبير الشيء على ما ينبغي أن يكون في التألف والتعديل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is physical: unlike other creatures, humans stand upright and use their hands to take food.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى خلق كل ذي روح مكبا على وجهه إلا الإنسان فإنه تعالى خلقه مديد القامة يتناول مأكوله بيده

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Aṣamm interprets the best form as complete intellect, understanding, manners, knowledge, and speech, covering inward character as well as outward form.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصم : في أكمل عقل وفهم وأدب

rows.speaker: يحيى بن أكثم
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Aktham takes the verse as proof of human beauty: a jurist who used the verse to answer a husband's oath said he was not legally in breach for preferring his wife to the moon.
rows.anchor: وعن يحيى بن أكثم القاضي أنه فسر التقويم بحسن الصورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pious person's prayer asks that the best outward forms granted in this world be matched by the best deeds in the next, namely forgiveness and pardon.
rows.anchor: وكان بعض الصالحين يقول : إلهنا أعطيتنا في الأولى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reads the lowest state as decrepit old age, when hearing, sight, reason, ability, and good works weaken.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد أرذل العمر

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains the low as the weak, chronically ill, helpless people who cannot find a way or means.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : السافلون هم الضعفاء والزمني

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ explains the plural سافلين despite singular الإنسان by treating humanity as a collective, like other singular nouns that denote a group.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : ولو كانت أسفل سافل لكان صوابا

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Hasan read the lowest state as Hell; ʿAli says its gates are stacked, with the lowest filled first.
rows.anchor: ما ذكره مجاهد والحسن ثم رددناه إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the old-age interpretation, the exception is disconnected: faithful elderly people receive lasting reward for obedience and patient worship despite the hardships and weakness of aging.
rows.anchor: هذا الاستثناء على القول الأول منقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Hell interpretation, the exception is connected to the preceding class.
rows.anchor: وأما على القول الثاني فالاستثناء متصل ظاهر الاتصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unending reward is either never diminished or cut off, or is given without reproach or reminding the recipient of favors.
rows.anchor: ففيه قولان : أحدهما : غير منقوص ولا مقطوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both qualities suit divine reward: it must neither end nor be tainted by reproach.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن كل ذلك من صفات الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Irya is bringing out fire and qadh is striking or clashing; the verse has several proposed subjects for the sparks.
rows.anchor: فاعلم أن الإيراء إخراج النار ، والقدح الصك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says horses strike mountains with their hooves and produce sparks like flint.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد ضرب الخيل بحوافرها الجبل

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the horses' hooves spark against stones like the fire of al-Habhab, a miser who lit fires only after people slept and extinguished them when they woke.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : يعني الخيل تقدحن بحوافرهن في الحجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A related explanation says iron horseshoes strike stone; the first view is stronger because it makes the horses' own hooves like iron.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من يقول : إنها نعل الحديد يصك الحجر فتخرج النار

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Others say the horses kindle the fires of war between their owners and enemies, as in the verse about God extinguishing the fire of war.
rows.anchor: قال قوم : هذه الآيات في الخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the sparks with fires lit by raiders at night for cooking and other needs; the striking horses are the raiding band.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : هم الذين يغزون فيورون بالليل نيرانهم لحاجتهم وطعامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other metaphorical readings are tongues kindling enmity and men's thoughts igniting deceit; Ibn ʿAbbas is cited for the latter, including fires lit to exaggerate an army's size.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : إنها هي الألسنة توري نار العداوة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says the sparks are made by spearheads.
rows.anchor: وسادسها : قال عكرمة : الموريات قدحا الأسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final view reads the phrase as people succeeding in a raid or pilgrimage; it could mean the successful group or its mounts, with a line by Jarir using the idiom of kindling a flint.
rows.anchor: وسابعها : { فالموريات قدحا } أي فالمنجحات أمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom قدح أورى means a strike that makes sparks, while the same root can metaphorically mean success; literal fire is preferred here.
rows.anchor: ويقال : فلان إذا قدح أورى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The default reading is horses attacking an enemy at dawn: it is too dark to see at night, while people are ready for battle during the day and inattentive at dawn.
rows.anchor: يعني الخيل تغير على العدو وقت الصبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who take the animals as camels say they carry pilgrims from Muzdalifa to Mina on the Sacrifice day, when the rite requires waiting until morning; إغارة means speed.
rows.anchor: وأما الذين حملوا هذه الآيات على الإبل ، قالوا : المراد هو الإبل

rows.speaker: العرب
rows.claim: The pre-Islamic Arabs said, Rise, Thabir, so that we may hasten onward, illustrating the sense of swift departure.
rows.anchor: وكانت العرب في الجاهلية تقول : أشرق ثبير كيما نغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نقع can mean dust, explained either by its rising or by the image of sinking into water; it can also mean funeral wailing, as in a prophetic report.
rows.anchor: في النقع قولان : أحدهما : أنا هو الغبار

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic saying uses نقع for mourning cries; in the context, the horses stir dust where they raid through their forceful charge.
rows.anchor: والثاني : النقع الصباح من قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( مالم يكن نقع ولا لقلقة )

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says به refers indirectly to the place where the raid ends, since the preceding phrase establishes that a raid must occur somewhere.
rows.anchor: أحدها : وهو قول الفراء أنه عائد إلى المكان الذي انتهى إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, به refers to the time when the attack took place.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : إنه عائد إلى ذلك الزمان الذي وقعت فيه الإغارة

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says به refers to the enemy, mentioned earlier in the oath.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : وهو قول الكسائي أنه عائد إلى العدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb فأثرن coordinates with the verbs implied by the preceding active participles: the mounts ran, sparked, raided, and then raised dust.
rows.anchor: على الفعل الذي وضع اسم الفاعل موضعه

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abu Haywa reads the verb with a doubled ث, meaning they brought out or displayed dust; the reading may also reflect a change from ثرن to وثرن and then hamza.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو حيوة : { فأثرن } بالتشديد بمعنى فأظهرن به غبارا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ takes موازين as weighed deeds, meaning actions that have weight and consequence with God.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه جمع موزون وهو العمل الذي له وزن وخطر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas takes موازين as scales with a tongue and two pans; good deeds appear beautiful and outweigh, while the unbeliever's ugly deeds are light.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : الميزان له لسان وكفتان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the scale has two pans but its nature is not described.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : في الميزان له كفتان ولا يوصف

rows.speaker: المتكلمون
rows.claim: Theologians say past good and bad acts cannot themselves be weighed; instead, written records, light and darkness, or beautiful and ugly forms of records display their weight.
rows.anchor: قال المتكلمون : إن نفس الحسنات والسيئات لا يصح وزنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weighing publicly reveals the righteous person's state and increases joy, while exposing the evildoer to humiliation before all creatures.
rows.anchor: وتكون الفائدة في ذلك ظهور حال صاحب الحسنات في الجمع العظيم فيزداد سرورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Light scales mean few good deeds, with wrongs outweighing right actions.
rows.anchor: أي قلت : حسناته فرجحت السيئات على الحسنات

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr says the scale grows heavy through following the weighty truth in life, and grows light through following falsehood.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر رضي الله عنه : إنما ثقلت موازين من ثقلت موازينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi relays Muqatils explanation that truth is heavy and falsehood light.
rows.anchor: لأن الحق ثقيل والباطل خفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilhāʾ is turning someone toward diversion; diversion follows desire and entails neglecting something else, so ألهاني means distracted or made me forget.
rows.anchor: الإلهاء الصرف إلى اللهو . واللهو الانصراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takāthur means boasting competitively about wealth, status, and distinctions; Abu Muslim says its morphology can express mutual competition, effort to increase, or simply becoming numerous.
rows.anchor: والتكاثر التباهي بكثرة المال والجاه والمناقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human happiness comprises the soul's knowledge and virtues, bodily health and beauty, and external goods such as wealth, status, relatives, and friends; external goods ultimately serve the body.
rows.anchor: وأجناس السعادة ثلاثة : فأحدها : في النفس والثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wise people should pursue bodily health for the sake of lasting spiritual happiness; competing for wealth and kinship elevates the lowest goods above knowledge and action.
rows.anchor: العاقل ينبغي أن يكون سعيه في تقديم الأهم على المهم ، فالتفاخر بالمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse condemns competition in every worldly pleasure, including numbers, wealth, status, relatives, supporters, and armies.
rows.anchor: ويدخل فيه التكاثر بالعدد وبالمال والجاه والأقرباء والأنصار والجيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ألهاكم can be a statement about the people's distraction or a reproachful question asking whether competition distracted them.
rows.anchor: قوله : { ألهاكم } يحتمل أن يكون إخبارا عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Competition is not always blameworthy: the verse about pilgrimage water and the Kaaba key reports rivals boasting over religious services before ʿAli's claim of fighting unbelief.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك ما روى من تفاخر العباس بأن السقاية بيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may display obedience and good character when it could encourage others; therefore competition in knowledge, devotion, and virtue is praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: أنه يجوز للإنسان أن يفتخر بطاعاته ومحاسن أخلاقه إذا كان يظن أن غيره يقتدي به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in التكاثر refers to familiar worldly accumulation, not every kind of striving; that distraction obstructs worship, while competition in virtue is good.
rows.anchor: فالألف واللام في التكاثر ليسا للاستغراق ، بل للمعهود السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says the verse concerns numerical rivalry between Banu Sahm and Banu ʿAbd Manaf; after counting living and dead people, Banu Sahm claimed the larger number.
rows.anchor: روى أنها نزلت في بني سهم وبني عبد مناف تفاخروا أيهم أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording حتى زرتم المقابر sounds like a completed event; the verse mocks the thought that merely outnumbering rivals has any benefit.
rows.anchor: وهذه الرواية مطابقة لظاهر القرآن ، لأن قوله : { حتى زرتم المقابر } يدل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report urges grave visits because they remind people of death; here the rivals visited graves because of hard hearts and immersion in worldly love.
rows.anchor: على ما قال عليه السلام : ( كنت نهيتكم عن زيارة القبور ألا فزوروها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the rivalry about wealth; a report from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir's father says a person's wealth is only what he consumed, wore, or gave away.
rows.anchor: استدلوا عليه بما روى مطرف بن عبد الله بن الشخير عن أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the wealth reading, visiting graves is a metaphor for dying; Jarir's line uses visiting graves to mean Abu Malik died.
rows.anchor: وزيارة القبر عبارة عن الموت ، يقال لمن مات : زار قبره وزار رمسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi raises two objections: visitors leave while the dead remain, and the past-tense wording seems incompatible with future death.
rows.anchor: يقال حمله على هذا الوجه مشكل من وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Replies say the dead too must leave for judgment; the address may concern people near death, earlier generations on whose path the living follow, or disbelievers on Judgment Day after their graves are visited.
rows.anchor: والجواب : عن السؤال الأول أنه قد يمكث الزائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes العصر as time or the age; a report says the Prophet swore by time, but al-Razi refuses to treat its wording as Qur'an because that would invalidate prayer.
rows.anchor: ما روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه أقسم بالدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Time contains astonishing opposites such as health and illness or wealth and poverty, and resists a simple account of existence because past and future are absent while the indivisible present cannot be divided.
rows.anchor: أن الدهر مشتمل على الأعاجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final moment of life can redeem a wasted thousand years through repentance and eternal salvation, so time is among the greatest blessings.
rows.anchor: فلو ضيعت ألف سنة ، ثم تبث في اللمحة الأخيرة من العمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day are opportunities to remember and give thanks; the Qur'an also connects time and what occupies it to God's dominion.
rows.anchor: فلذلك أقسم به ونبه على أن الليل والنهار فرصة يضيعها المكلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs blamed misfortune on time, but the oath teaches that time is a blessing and the human being who wastes it is at fault.
rows.anchor: أنهم كانوا يضيفون الخسران إلى نوائت الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As each age passes, life shrinks; unless a person gains something in return, the loss of lifespan is itself a loss.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى ذكر العصر الذي بمضيه ينتقص عمرك

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim reads العصر as one end of the day, the afternoon, paired with the morning's signs of resurrection, judgment, and the evening's signs of death and destruction.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أبي مسلم : المراد بالعصر أحد طرفي النهار

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says afternoon signals that markets are closing: whoever has failed to earn must face dependents and creditors, a picture of the approaching Judgment and unprepared worldly life.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن رحمه الله : إنما أقسم بهذا الوقت

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says that one who swears falsely after the afternoon prayer will face God's displeasure and lack of regard on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : ( من حلف بعد العصر كاذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As midmorning in the previous sura assures the righteous of rising fortunes, the afternoon oath warns the doomed of decline; its remaining daylight urges repentance.
rows.anchor: فكما أقسم في حق الرابح بالضحى فكذا أقسم في حق الخاسر بالعصر

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: A seller of ice taught a student the sura's meaning by crying, Pity the one whose capital melts: age passes without gain and leaves its owner at a loss.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض السلف : تعلمت معنى السورة من بائع الثلج
